text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing monotonic host RAM growth on Dedicated when running long-context chats (>=8k tokens). Hosted clusters show flat curves for same workload. link to profile: https://internal/profiles/1768504321

morgan: Can you share jemalloc stats + model/quant config?

alex: Same model + quant: redwood-m1-13b-q4, batching unchanged. Quick jemalloc dump: ```allocated: 3.2G
active: 4.1G
metadata: 128M
retained: 512M
arenas: 2
tcache: 64M```

tessa: Dedicated nodes are on kernel 5.15 + cgroupv1; Hosted is 6.1 + cgroupv2. Different mmap/madvise semantics and default hugepage/THP settings can change fragmentation/evict behavior.

jin: We also see lots of kvcache backfill logs on Dedicated: `EVICT slot=9823 frame=...` — fragments are being reconstituted rather than reused. Paging spikes match backfill windows.

morgan: Are you seeing PGMAJOR or swap churn? Any OOM cgroup events?

alex: No OOM kills. dmesg shows repeated page allocation slowdowns and PGMAJOR faults: `kernel: page allocation failure, order:0, mode:MA` starting at 1768504402. Hosted has very few PGMAJOR events.

tessa: Another interesting find: config drift alert shows kv.cache_enabled=false on Dedicated (probable cause) vs true on Hosted. If cache isn't preserving prefixes, we end up allocating new frames and fragmenting.

morgan: That would explain reuse delta. Try enabling kv.cache_enabled for a small canary on Dedicated and run the same long-context replay.

alex: Did a quick canary toggle to true on one pool. Growth slope flattened within 20 minutes. Reuse hit-rate went from ~28% to ~73%.

jin: Nice. Still want to rule out kernel interaction — can you capture /proc/vmstat, /proc/zoneinfo and jemalloc profs for the canary period? Also check hugetlb and THP status.

tessa: Also add `mallctl` decay_time and background_thread tweaks for jemalloc in the canary — fragmentation dropped in a previous test when we shortened decay time.

alex: Will run a 48h canary: kv.cache_enabled=true + jemalloc decay tweak + capture vmstats every 10m. Posting logs to the profile link.

morgan: If this reproduces, we should: 1) add config checksum enforcement for Dedicated onboarding, 2) include kernel tunable gating in our post-rolling checks, and 3) add a kvcache regression eval for long-context traces.

jin: I'll open INF ticket and schedule a short kernel parity test (spin up a Dedicated node with kernel 6.1 if infra allows) to rule out kernel-only causes.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-4827: "compare kernel/tunables + kv config across Hosted/Dedicated/Private" (assigned to jin).

tessa: One more note — Private/on-prem GPUs we saw similar growth when NUMA balancing was off and NVLink topology differed. Might need a separate repro for on-prem.

alex: Good call. I'll include an on-prem trace sample in the ticket.

morgan: Thanks team. If canary holds, let's roll the config fix to the rest of Dedicated and add the checksum guard. :thumbsup:
